newsitem.title: MEXICO: La Moderna reports Q1 1997 earnings. [CORRECTED 20:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: La Moderna reports Q1 1997 earnings. [CORRECTED 20:45 GMT]

text.p: Mexico's Empresas La Moderna, a conglomorate with major tobacco and vegetable seed interests, reported a net consolidated profit of 660 million pesos for the first quarter of 1997 compared with 667 million pesos in the first quarter of last year.

The company said in a news releases that its net consolidated profits takes into account earnings derived from extraordinary operations such as the partial sale of its Asgrow and Empaques Ponderosa (Empaq) subsidiaries (corrects to show that only portions of subsidiaries were sold).
The net majority income was 427.3 million pesos in the first quarter of this year compared with 575.55 million in the same period a year ago, La Moderna said.
Sales reached 2.971 billion peosos, seven percent lower than in the first quarter of 1996, the company said.
The decrease was mainly a reflection of "applying Mexican accounting principles to a companies whose income is largely in foreign currency," La Moderna said.
Sales in foreign currency equalled $157 million or 42 percent of the total, La Moderna said.

Consolidated operating income was 226 million pesos, lower than the 392 million reported a year earlier, mostly due to lower sales volumes in cigarettes and seeds as well as a stronger peso, La Moderna said.

The company's debt fell to $706 million at the end of Q1 1997 compared to $906 million after the fourth quarter of 1996. La Moderna said it was able to sharply lower its debt load though the sale of its subsidiaries.
